title: The N2 Middle: Torre, Schist Villages and the Road South
subRegion: Beira Interior, Serra da Estrela & the Alentejo Guadiana

bestPeriod.avoid: December-March for the Torre road (snow closures, chains, and weekend snow-tourist gridlock) and August, when the Alentejo run south hits 40 °C and the schist villages fill

accommodation.note: Rural guesthouse double €70, €120 per room; Piódão and Monsanto book out fast

food.note: Beira menu do dia €9, €14; Alentejo dinner €18, €28; Serra cheese to take home

transport.note: Car hire €200, €350/week, fuel ≈€120, tolls ≈€40, Via Verde device €10, €18

activities.note: Museums, Belmonte Jewish Museum, Mértola sites, N2 passport €1.50

profile.difficultyNote: 2/5, driving plus short steep village walks; Piódão, Monsanto and Talasnal all require walking up on cobbles

gatewayAirport: OPO Porto, 1 h 30 min to Viseu; LIS Lisbon 2 h 20 min to Viseu; exit from FAO Faro, 1 h 30 min from Mértola
summary: The **Estrada Nacional 2** runs 738 km from Chaves on the Spanish border to Faro on the Algarve coast, crossing 35 municipalities, Portugal's Route 66, and unlike the American one, it is still the road. This week takes its central section and deliberately leaves it three times: east over the **Serra da Estrela** to Torre at 1,993 m and down the glacial Zêzere valley, east again to the granite border villages of Belmonte, Sortelha and Monsanto, and west into the schist of Piódão and the Serra da Lousã. Then it commits to the N2 proper for a long, hypnotic run south through the Alentejo to Mértola on the Guadiana. It is a driver's week: 1,100-1,200 km, a lot of second gear, and a stamp collected in every town.

itinerary.title: Viseu: pick up the car, pick up the passport
itinerary.morning: Fly into Porto, collect the car, **confirm the Via Verde transponder is fitted and active before you leave the lot**, and drive to **Viseu**, 130 km on the A25, about 1 h 30.
itinerary.afternoon: Viseu's granite old town: the **Sé Catedral**, the **Museu Grão Vasco** for Vasco Fernandes's 16th-century panels, and the Rua Direita. Buy the **N2 passport** at the tourist office and take your first stamp.
itinerary.evening: Dão wine, this is its capital, with roast kid or *bacalhau*. Sit in Praça de Dom Duarte.
itinerary.dayStats: OPO→Viseu 130 km / 1 h 30 on the A25 (electronic tolls); Viseu ≈480 m; passport €1.50; stamps collected: 1

itinerary.title: N2 to Seia, then the N339 to Torre
itinerary.morning: South on the **N2** through Nelas to **Seia**, 55 km in a genuine hour. Stamp at Seia. **Fill the tank here**, there is no fuel over the top.
itinerary.afternoon: The **N339** to **Torre, 1,993 m**, 25 km and a full hour of climbing past **Sabugueiro**, at ≈1,050 m the highest village in Portugal, onto a bare granite plateau of glacial lakes and wind. The summit has a stone obelisk, a cluster of shops and, in winter, Portugal's only ski lifts. Check the weather before you commit and turn back if the cloud is down.
itinerary.evening: Descend to Seia or push on to **Manteigas**. Eat **Queijo Serra da Estrela DOP**, the raw ewe's-milk cheese set with thistle rennet, spooned out of the top of the wheel, with dark bread.
itinerary.dayStats: 80 km / 2 h driving; Seia ≈500 m → Torre 1,993 m in 25 km; stamps: 2-3
itinerary.sleep: Manteigas, small hotel or *casa de campo*

itinerary.title: The Vale do Zêzere, Covão da Ametade and Poço do Inferno
itinerary.morning: Be at **Covão da Ametade at first light**, the head of the glacial valley at ≈1,400 m, birches, a stream, and the granite prow of **Cântaro Magro** above. Then drive the **N338 down the Vale do Zêzere**, a textbook U-shaped glacial trough 13 km long, with the road on the shelf above it.
itinerary.afternoon: From **Manteigas (720 m)**, the forest road to **Poço do Inferno**, narrow, rough, and closed often enough that you should check locally first. Then the **Penhas Douradas** plateau road for the high-moor light.
itinerary.evening: Manteigas is a one-street mountain town in a deep valley; the light goes early. Trout from the Zêzere, and an early night.
itinerary.dayStats: 60 km / 2 h driving; Nave de Santo António ≈1,530 m; Vale do Zêzere 13 km; Manteigas 720 m
itinerary.sleep: Manteigas, small hotel or *casa de campo*

itinerary.title: Granite border villages: Belmonte, Sortelha, Monsanto
itinerary.morning: Down the N232 and east to **Belmonte**, the Cabral family's castle, the **Museu Judaico** telling the story of the crypto-Jewish community that kept its faith in secret for four centuries, and the Roman tower of **Centum Cellas** just outside town.
itinerary.afternoon: **Sortelha**, a completely walled granite village on a rock outcrop, entered through a low gate; park outside and walk the walls at golden hour. Then east to **Monsanto**, where the houses are built under, over and between granite boulders the size of buses, with the Templar castle above.
itinerary.evening: Monsanto's castle at sunset, looking into Spain. Dinner in the village; there are only a handful of kitchens and they close early.
itinerary.dayStats: 120 km / 2 h 30 driving; Monsanto ≈760 m; village is car-free, 10 min walk up from the car park; stamps: +2
itinerary.sleep: Monsanto, small guesthouse in the village

itinerary.title: Castelo Branco, then west to the schist
itinerary.morning: South to **Castelo Branco**, 50 km, for the **Jardim do Paço Episcopal**, a Baroque garden of clipped box and granite statuary where the kings of the Spanish occupation are carved deliberately smaller than the rest. Best in morning light.
itinerary.afternoon: The long westward leg back across the N2 corridor via Sertã and Góis into the **Serra do Açor**, finishing on the single-track **M1441** to **Piódão**. Take it slowly; there are passing places and blind hairpins and nowhere to go if you meet a van.
itinerary.evening: **Piódão** at dusk and again after dark, a schist village stacked in an amphitheatre, every door and window frame painted the same blue, floodlit at night. Eat *chanfana* or goat.
itinerary.dayStats: 200 km / 3 h 30 driving; fuel at Arganil or Góis; Piódão ≈700 m, car-free core

itinerary.title: Talasnal and the Serra da Lousã, then down to the N2
itinerary.morning: North-west over the mountain to the **Serra da Lousã** and **Talasnal**, the best restored of the *aldeias do xisto*, schist walls, slate roofs, no cars, and a handful of houses brought back from complete abandonment. **Casal Novo** and **Chiqueiro** nearby are still half-ruined and worth the extra half hour.
itinerary.afternoon: Down to Lousã and east to rejoin the **N2** near Vila de Rei, then south to **Abrantes** on the Tejo. Collect stamps as you go.
itinerary.evening: Abrantes castle terrace over the river. This is the hinge of the trip: mountains behind, plains ahead.
itinerary.dayStats: 165 km / 3 h driving; Talasnal ≈800 m, final approach on foot; stamps: +3-4

itinerary.title: The long N2 south to Mértola
itinerary.morning: The N2 proper, and a lot of it: **Ponte de Sor, Montargil, Mora, Pavia**, through cork oak and holm oak *montado* with red earth beneath. Stop where the marker posts are; stamp where there is a café.
itinerary.afternoon: **Ferreira do Alentejo, Aljustrel, Castro Verde**, then east on the N123 to **Mértola**, a walled hill town over the Guadiana where the parish church is a converted mosque with its mihrab still in the wall, above a Roman and Islamic archaeological site.
itinerary.evening: The castle keep at sunset over the river, then Alentejo cooking, *ensopado de borrego*, *migas*, and a bottle of Alentejano red.
itinerary.dayStats: 330 km / 4 h 45-5 h 15 driving; fuel at Ponte de Sor; Mértola→FAO 1 h 30 for the flight home; total week ≈1,150 km

accommodationStrategy.name: A *casa de campo* in Manteigas
accommodationStrategy.description: The only sensible base for two nights in the mountains: it puts Covão da Ametade twenty minutes away for a first-light start and means you drive the Zêzere valley twice rather than once. Choose somewhere with off-street parking, because Manteigas's streets are steep and narrow, and somewhere with heating, it is cold at 720 m in a deep valley well into June. €70, €120 per room.

accommodationStrategy.name: A village guesthouse in Monsanto
accommodationStrategy.description: Staying in Monsanto rather than day-tripping it is the whole difference: the coach visitors leave by six, and the village at sunset and at dawn belongs to about eighty residents and you. Accept that you will carry bags ten minutes uphill from the car park on stone lanes. €70, €110 per room, and it books out weeks ahead.

accommodationStrategy.name: A schist house in Piódão
accommodationStrategy.description: Same logic. Piódão is a day-trip destination for coaches out of Coimbra, and a completely different place after dark when it is floodlit and empty. Rooms are small, the walls are slate, and the parking is the public lot below. €65, €110 per room. Book early, there are very few beds.

logistics.connectivity: EU roaming applies. 4G is good in the towns and along the N2, patchy in the Zêzere valley and on the Torre plateau, and genuinely poor on the single-track approaches to Piódão and Talasnal. Download offline maps for the whole Beira Interior, the M-numbered mountain roads are badly signed and some navigation apps will route you onto forest tracks.
logistics.emergency: **112** for everything. Mountain incidents in the Serra da Estrela are handled by the **GNR** and the ANEPC civil protection service; response into the Zêzere valley or off the Torre plateau is slow. Portugal is in the EU, so **EHIC/GHIC covers state treatment**; the referral hospitals are Covilhã and Castelo Branco in the north of the route, Beja in the south.
logistics.weather: The Serra da Estrela makes its own weather. Fog banks form on the western scarp with almost no warning and reduce the N339 to walking pace; freezing fog is common in autumn. Snow can fall on Torre in any month from October to May. The Alentejo is the opposite problem: 38-42 °C in July and August with no shade on the N2 and a real risk of tyre failure on hot tarmac. Autumn brings dense valley fog before 10:00 across the Beira.
logistics.bookingWindows: Piódão and Monsanto rooms **4-8 weeks ahead**, more for a weekend, because both have only a handful of beds. Manteigas 2-4 weeks. Car hire with a one-way Porto/Lisbon-Faro drop should be booked **2-3 months ahead**, both for price and because one-way availability is limited. Restaurants generally need no booking outside August.
logistics.money: Euro. Cards work almost everywhere including village cafés, though Portugal's domestic **Multibanco** system means some small machines reject foreign cards, carry €80, €100 cash. Fuel stations in villages may be attended-only and closed on Sundays. Tipping is 5-10% or rounding up.
logistics.transportRules: **The electronic-toll issue is the single biggest practical trap in Portugal.** The **A23**, **A22**, **A24**, **A25** and other former SCUT roads have no booths, you need a **Via Verde transponder** (take the rental firm's, €1.50, €2.50/day) or a registered EASYToll/TollCard/TollService arrangement, or you accumulate fines. Conventional motorways with barriers accept cards. Cross-border driving into Spain needs the rental company's written permission and usually a fee. Headlights are not required by day, but a reflective vest and warning triangle are mandatory in the car.
logistics.permits: The **Parque Natural da Serra da Estrela** is a protected area, no wild camping, no off-road driving, and fire restrictions from May to October that can close forest roads entirely. Drones need ANAC registration and are restricted over the park and over settlements. Foraging is limited; the Serra's *queijo* and honey are best bought, not gathered.
logistics.health: Tap water is potable throughout, including in the villages. Summer **wildfire risk is severe** in the schist and pine country around Piódão, Góis and Lousã, the 2017 fires here killed dozens, and roads are closed at short notice during red-alert days; check ipma.pt and the ANEPC alerts daily in July-September. Ticks in the *montado*. At Torre, remember it is 1,993 m: sun burns fast and wind chill can be 15 °C below the valley temperature.

proTips: **Sort the Via Verde transponder at the rental desk, and test it at the first gantry.** A week of unpaid electronic tolls arrives as fines at your home address months later, with administration charges from the rental firm on top.

**Buy the N2 passport on day one in Viseu, not later.** Stamps are collected at tourist offices, cafés and hotels, and half the fun is asking a café owner in Mora whether they stamp, they do, and they are pleased to.

**Check the Torre road before you drive to Seia.** GNR and the park authority close the N339 and N338 at short notice for snow, ice and fog, and the closure is enforced at barriers below the summit. In marginal conditions, chains are compulsory and turnbacks are routine.
**Do Covão da Ametade at dawn and Cântaro Magro in late afternoon**, the same valley, two completely different photographs, and neither works in the flat midday light most visitors get.
**Sleep in the small villages, day-trip the big towns.** Monsanto and Piódão are transformed after the coaches leave; Castelo Branco and Viseu are the same whenever you go.

**Fill the tank three times without thinking about it:** Seia before Torre, Arganil or Góis before Piódão, Ponte de Sor before the Alentejo run. Rural stations shut on Sundays and evenings and the gaps are longer than they look.
**Drive the single-track M1441 to Piódão with the window down.** You will hear an oncoming car before you see it, and there are passing places roughly every 200 m, note the last one you passed.

**Budget the final day honestly.** Abrantes to Mértola on the N2 is roughly 330 km of single carriageway through villages with 50 km/h limits. It is five hours plus stops, not three, and the GNR speed enforcement on the Alentejo straights is relentless.

**Eat Queijo Serra da Estrela DOP properly.** Buy a whole wheel in Seia or Manteigas between November and April, cut the top off like a lid, and spoon it. Outside those months you are eating last season's, cured harder.

**If you fall for it, come back for the other 400 km.** Chaves to Viseu in the north and Almodôvar to Faro in the south are each a comfortable long weekend, and the passport is designed to make you finish it.

raw.Viseu → Seia, N2 via Nelas and Santa Com: Good two-lane road, some slow village sections. This is real N2, marker posts included.
raw.Seia → Torre, N339, 25 km, 50-60 min: Continuous climb from ≈500 m to **1,993 m**. Surfaced and well maintained but narrow above the treeline, with no barrier in places and a bare, wind-scoured summit plateau. Not a 25-minute drive, ever.
raw.Torre → Manteigas via Nave de Santo Antó: The finest 30 km in mainland Portugal. Single carriageway, granite boulders at the verge, blind bends, ice in shadow into April.
raw.Manteigas → Belmonte, N232 then N18, 35: Steep descent off the Serra, then easy.
raw.Belmonte → Sortelha → Monsanto, N18 / N2: Rolling granite country, slow and empty.
raw.Monsanto → Castelo Branco → Góis → Piódã: The last 20 km into Piódão is single-track with passing places.
raw.Abrantes → Mértola on the N2 proper via: Long straights, almost no traffic, and nowhere near as fast as the map implies.
raw.Torre, 1,993 m: , the highest point in mainland Portugal, marked by a stone obelisk raised to make it a round 2,000 m. Reached by the **N339** from Seia in the west or from Covilhã via **Penhas da Saúde (≈1,500 m)** in the east.
raw.Nave de Santo António, ≈1,530 m: , the plateau junction where the Zêzere descent begins.
raw.Covão da Ametade, ≈1,400 m: , the head of the glacial valley under the granite face of **Cântaro Magro**.
raw.Poço do Inferno, ≈1,050 m: , a waterfall reached by a narrow forest road out of Manteigas that is regularly closed by fire damage or rockfall.
raw.Seasonal reality: the roads to Torre are **routinely closed by snow and ice at short notice between December and March**, and closures have occurred as late as May after unseasonal falls. When conditions require it, **snow chains are mandatory** and the GNR turns back cars without them at the barriers below the summit. Even in open conditions, expect fog banks above 1,400 m at any time of year and freezing fog in autumn. Winter weekends bring snow-tourist traffic that gridlocks the Torre car park and the N339 behind it. **Do not plan this itinerary between December and March without an alternative for Days 2 and 3.**
notes: Portugal's former SCUT motorways are **electronic-only with no toll booths at all**, the **A23 Beira Interior** (Castelo Branco-Covilhã-Guarda) is the one this route touches, and the **A22** in the Algarve if you exit via Faro. Driving them without a registered payment method generates a fine, not a bill.

Take the rental company's **Via Verde transponder**: typically **€1.50, €2.50 per day** on top of the tolls themselves, and it works at every barrier and gantry in the country. The alternatives, **EASYToll** (register a card at an automatic booth near the border), **TollCard** and **TollService**, exist but are fiddly and time-limited.
raw.Cross-border into Spain: is normally permitted by Portuguese rental firms with notice and a modest fee; check the contract, because Monsanto and Sortelha sit within 30 km of the frontier and a wrong turn onto a Spanish motorway is easy. Via Verde is interoperable with Spain's Via-T on much of the network but do not rely on it.
raw.One-way drops are expensive: Picking up at Porto or Lisbon and dropping at Faro typically costs **€60, €150**, plus an airport surcharge each end. Budget for it, the alternative is a 500 km repositioning drive.
raw.Fuel gaps to plan for: nothing between **Seia and Manteigas** over the top (fill in Seia); nothing on the **Piódão approach** (fill in Arganil or Góis); and long empty stretches on the **N2 between Mora and Ferreira do Alentejo** (fill in Ponte de Sor). Many rural stations close on Sundays and after 20:00.
raw.Torre summit plateau: , mid-morning, before the cloud builds on the western scarp.
raw.Cântaro Magro from the N338 above Covão: , **late afternoon**, when low sun rakes the granite face.
raw.Covão da Ametade: , **first light**, for mist sitting in the valley floor under the birches.
raw.Vale do Zêzere from the N338 hairpins ab: , **late afternoon**; the U-shaped profile only reads properly with shadow in it.
raw.Monsanto castle: , **sunset**, looking out over the plain toward Spain.
raw.Sortelha walls: , **golden hour**, when the granite goes orange.
raw.The Piódão viewpoint on the M1441 approa: , **late afternoon**, and again after dark when the village is floodlit and the blue-painted doors show.
raw.Parking realities, town by town: **Viseu**, historic core is pedestrian; use the paid underground or the free surface parking near the Cava de Viriato and walk in. **Seia**, easy and free. **Manteigas**, steep, narrow, one-way; park along the N232 at the top of the village. **Monsanto**, **you cannot drive into the village**; the lanes squeeze between house-sized granite boulders. Park in the lot below and walk up, ten minutes, steeply. **Sortelha**, park outside the walls. **Piódão**, a designated car park below the village; the settlement itself is car-free and the approach road is single-track. **Talasnal**, park on the road above and walk the last few hundred metres. **Castelo Branco**, paid parking near Praça do Município. **Mértola**, park by the river below the walls.
raw.Portuguese driving hazards specific to t: Serra da Estrela sheep flocks on the N339 and N338, guarded by **Cão da Serra da Estrela** dogs that do not move for cars. Motorcyclists cutting the apex on Torre hairpins at weekends. Black ice in shaded Zêzere corners from October to April. **Single-track roads to Piódão and Talasnal** where local drivers take blind bends at speed, sound the horn. Autumn fog in the Beira Interior basins, dense enough to close visibility to 30 m before 10:00. In the Alentejo, long unlit straights that induce speeding into **heavy GNR radar enforcement**, fines are payable on the spot by non-residents, plus **wild boar and deer at dusk** and cork-oak lorries. Limits are 50 urban / 90 rural / 100 dual carriageway / 120 motorway; blood alcohol 0.5 g/l, and 0.2 for drivers licensed under three years.
raw.The N2 passport ritual: Buy the **Passaporte Rota da Estrada Nacional 2** for around **€1.50** from the Associação Rota da EN2 (rotan2.pt) or from tourist offices on the route. It has a page for each of the **35 municipalities** the road crosses, and you collect stamps at **tourist offices, cafés and accommodation** along the way. Do the whole 738 km Chaves-Faro and it earns a certificate. On a central-section week you will fill perhaps ten to fourteen pages, which is precisely the point, you come back for the rest.

sources.verified: The **Passaporte Rota da Estrada Nacional 2** sold by the Associação Rota da EN2 at **€1.50**, covering the **35 municipalities** the N2 crosses, with stamps collected at tourist offices, cafés and accommodation along the route. Reporting confirming that the **Serra da Estrela road to Torre is closed by snow at short notice, including out-of-season late-spring closures**, and that access is controlled when conditions require.
sources.confidenceNotes: Re-verify before publishing, (1) **current N339/N338 status and any barrier or chain requirement** for the dates of travel, via the Parque Natural da Serra da Estrela, the GNR or the Seia and Manteigas municipalities; this is the itinerary's biggest single point of failure. (2) The **Poço do Inferno forest road**, which has been closed repeatedly by fire damage and rockfall, check locally in Manteigas rather than trusting a map. (3) **Toll product names, daily transponder charges and the EASYToll/TollCard/TollService options**, which Infraestruturas de Portugal and the rental firms revise periodically. (4) **One-way drop fees** Porto/Lisbon → Faro, which vary hugely by operator and season and were not quoted from a live booking. (5) All **drive times**, estimated deliberately on the pessimistic side but not driven this run; the Abrantes-Mértola leg in particular should be sanity-checked. (6) **Sunday and evening fuel-station opening** in Sabugueiro, Arganil, Góis and along the Alentejo N2. (7) **Museum and site opening days** for the Belmonte Jewish Museum, the Jardim do Paço in Castelo Branco and the Mértola archaeological sites, several of which close on Mondays. (8) The frequently repeated claim that **Alvaiázere marks the midpoint of the EN2** is a local designation rather than a surveyed fact, and is not relied on above. (9) Accommodation rates throughout are indicative shoulder-season figures, not quotes.
